answer: Each key must receive a tracked postcard carrying a one-time orchard/ridge/ripple code at a previously unused delivery address; the recipient scans it within 10 days. The registry consumes both tracking ID and address token, rejects duplicates or expired codes, and suspends a key if the carrier delivery record is reversed. Proposed postage and validation fee: .60 per identity, not a live protocol rule. One honest agent pays .60 once; 1,000 fakes at distinct addresses cost ,600 (1,000 × .60). Limitation: shared households and postal coverage make access unequal.
